5 February 2030; Week Four of Instruction

Grand Kru County, Liberia

Thomas Edward Lawrence Military Academy, SASSTOWN

The mid-morning sun pierced through the sheer curtains of the Year 8 classroom. Seventy-five boys sat quietly, nearly holding their breath. Their white linen shirts contrasted with their smooth skin, dark as chocolate. The heavy wooden desks were arranged as an amphitheatre in three levels. At the bottom level, a man paced back and forth in front of a blackboard as he spoke.

"ah Umlaut", spoke the blond-haired professor, quickly and accurately snapping his pointing stick to the letter on the board. The wood struck the slate, producing a sharp cracking sound.

A chorus of voices echoed his: "ah Umlaut!"

"Beh." Again the tip of the wooden stick touched the board.

"Beh!", seventy-five boys replied. They smiled, showing off their gleaming white teeth as they waited for the next letter to be read.

This continued through the rest of the German alphabet, and the whole process was then repeated again several times.

"Very good, lads." The German man's accent was barely perceptible. He wiped the smallest of drops of sweat from his brow, marked by his many years and yet not completely wrinkled. Even before noon in February, the tropical heat could be felt. "Now, we shall practice our vocabulary. Repeat after me: ..."

For another twenty minutes, the lesson continued. "I think it's nearly time-"

Bronze striking bronze rang out through the campus, cutting his sentence short. Ten times the bell tolled, signalling the time. The whole world, save for the bell, seemed almost non-existent.

"Thank you, lads. Now off you go to your swimming instruction."

"Thank you Herr Adler!" The boys scurried out of the classroom and headed for the pool.
